title: Why classes provide different constructors
answer: Different constructors support different legitimate initialization scenarios while keeping invariants inside the class. One constructor may provide sensible defaults, while another accepts complete caller-supplied state. AeroTopo's `Product(String id)` supplies an empty tile list and delegates to `Product(String id, List<String> tiles)`, so callers can choose a concise default path or a more detailed creation path without duplicating initialization logic.
